answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds impose a convex, time-varying collateral that rises with each additional identity, while subgame-perfect punishment matrices specify off-equilibrium penalties that make any deviation strictly unprofitable; together they force every rational player to remain truthful, yielding a strict Nash equilibrium against Sybil multiplication as the terrace of capital barriers and the timber of credible threats converge, leaving an inlet of residual risk vanishing.
